comment: D-SINK-19. state.json's `activeKey`: which source is active, by key, in the
plugin's own 0600 file instead of as a provider URL in the host's shell.json.
Run by BOTH tests/Model.test.js and tests/test_state.py, because the rule is
implemented twice -- Model.activeKeyText / parseState in QML JS, and
normalize_active_key / normalize_state in the helper -- and a rule in two
languages gets one fixture (engineering rule 12, dev branch). The helper is the
half that matters most here: it REBUILDS the document from default_state() and
copies the keys it knows, so a key it has not been taught is ERASED by the next
`state favorite add`, and for THIS key that means the plugin reads as not
configured at all. savedSearches and hiddenGroups both carry that warning; this
one would have been visible.
`parse` cases: the raw JSON value of `activeKey` and the string both readers
must produce. A key naming no record is KEPT at parse time on purpose: whether
it resolves is a property of the LIST, not of the value, and dropping it here
would hide the case the migration has to decide about (Model.activeKeyOf is
where the resolution happens, and `resolve` below is the JavaScript-only half
that exercises it).
`resolve` and `adopt` cases are JavaScript only: the helper never resolves the
active source and never migrates one, because the migration reads the host's
bar entry and this helper knows nothing about shell.json by design (D15).

parse.name: absent reads as no active source
a three-digit suffix is the widest the grammar admits
surrounding whitespace is trimmed, not refused
an empty string is no active source
uppercase hex is not a key (the writers emit lowercase)
seven hex characters is not a key
nine hex characters is not a key
a four-digit suffix is not a key
a path traversal is not a key, which is what keeps it out of a directory name
a slash is not a key
a key with an interior space is not a key
a URL is not a key, and this is the shape a hand-edited old file would carry
a number is not a key
a boolean is not a key
a list is not a key
an object is not a key

resolveNote: Model.activeKeyOf: the stored key, but only while it names a record the same state carries. The dangling cases are the ones a CLI `state source remove`, an eviction and a hand-edited file all produce.

resolve.name: dangling: the record it named is gone
not a key, with a record that would otherwise match nothing
